judged_text: With sharing enabled accessTokenParsed.data contains only {access_token, refresh_token: 'refresh_token'} (the minimum schema strips the rest), so the persisted key loses instance_url, id, issued_at, signature, scope and token_type. The next jsforce.Connection is built with instanceUrl undefined, so subsequent Salesforce API calls target the wrong base URL and the integration fails after the first refresh under sharing mode.

adjudication.rationale: In `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` it validates using `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (which does not include fields like `instance_url`, `id`, `issued_at`, `signature`, `scope`, `token_type`) and Zod `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default. In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed token is persisted via `data: { key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token } }`, so under sharing mode the stored credential key would lose those extra Salesforce fields. On subsequent runs, `credential.key` would no longer contain `instance_url`, making `jsforce.Connection` construction prone to `instanceUrl` being undefined and breaking API calls.
